title: How Investors May Respond To Amazon Stock As AWS Growth And Anthropic IPO Near
detail:
How Investors May Respond To Amazon Stock As AWS Growth And Anthropic IPO Near
Bailey Pemberton
Fri, November 13, 2026 at 10:08 AM PST 5 min read
ANTH.PVT
AMZN
Trade AMZN on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Recent updates around Amazon.com highlight rapid momentum in AWS, expanding AI infrastructure spending, and growing commercial ties such as Anthropic and new satellite and cloud partnerships.

A key nuance is that much of Amazon's recent profit lift reflects mark-to-market gains on its Anthropic stake rather than cash earnings from AWS, retail, or advertising.

This article examines how Amazon's investment narrative is influenced by AWS's AI-driven growth and its sizable Anthropic exposure.

Spot 53 AI infrastructure stocks that could benefit from the same AI and cloud infrastructure momentum reshaping Amazon.com's AWS and Anthropic story.

Amazon.com Investment Narrative Recap

To own Amazon.com today, you need to be comfortable with a business that is trading current free cash flow for very heavy AI and cloud infrastructure spending. According to rcb9, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the real hinge is whether AWS revenue and cash generation arrive fast enough to absorb depreciation from roughly US$220b of annual capex. In the near term, the key catalyst is still AWS execution and backlog conversion, while the main risk is prolonged cash outflow if that build does not monetize as planned.

The latest Anthropic news adds another twist. Reported net income is already heavily influenced by mark to market gains on that stake, so Anthropic's IPO and post listing price swings could keep pulling Amazon's bottom line away from what the underlying operations are doing. That does not change the operational story around AWS capacity and retail efficiency, but it does raise the chance of headline earnings volatility that obscures whether the core business is actually progressing against those cash flow checkpoints rcb9 laid out.

The recent agreement that makes Can Marine Systems an authorized reseller for Amazon Leo is one of the clearest operational links to the current narrative. It shows Amazon.com trying to extend its cloud and AI infrastructure footprint into connectivity itself, using a low Earth orbit satellite network to reach customers that sit outside traditional fiber and cellular coverage. For AWS, every new distribution route for bandwidth and compute can become another on ramp for workload demand.

That satellite push also comes with its own execution questions. Amazon Leo involves thousands of satellites, ground infrastructure and third party partners like Can Marine, so service quality, uptime and economics will matter for whether this becomes a meaningful contributor or stays more experimental. For investors watching catalysts, the focus stays on whether projects like Leo and the Anthropic cloud commitments turn today's capex and paper gains into durable, high margin cash earnings over the next few years.

Why Amazon leads

Valuation: Its 21.5x P/E as of Sep 30, 2026, is well below Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) at 52.5x as of Aug 31, 2026. That gives Amazon more earnings-growth protection if sentiment cools.
